subject: Gateway Analytics PoC — demo pushed out as company reprioritizes
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@gatewayanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Healy <tom.healy@gatewayanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Gateway PoC — timeline update

Jonas,

Quick update from our side — leadership just announced a sprint-level freeze on new AI initiatives for Q3 while they shore up a couple of higher-priority platform migrations. Practically that means we need to push the PoC/demo conversations out for now; the key decision makers who were going to join your demo are traveling and won't be back in a decisioning cadence until October.

I know this is disappointing, and it isn't a "no" — more a timing shift. Can we park the demo for now and re-open the schedule in early October? If you have any short exec materials or a one-pager that helps us keep the value case warm, please send them along.

Also attaching a short internal note summarizing the reprioritization (internal).

Best,
Elena
Head of Data Products
Gateway Analytics

[Attachment: Gateway_internal_priority_note.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@gatewayanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway PoC — timeline update

Elena — thanks for the heads-up and congrats on keeping priorities tight. Totally understand the timing shift.

On our side, we'd be happy to:
- Park the demo and tentatively aim for an October touchpoint (I can send a Doodle in mid-Sept).
- Leave a small sandbox active so your team can poke at a sample dataset if that helps maintain momentum (we can dial access down until you want to ramp).
- Offer a modest pilot credit to keep procurement conversations warm when you re-engage (happy to propose terms).

If it helps with internal communications, I'll also send a one-page that calls out expected latency/unit-cost and sample prompts tailored to your use case.

I'll follow up internally and propose a low-friction nurture plan. Thanks again — we'll stay available and flexible.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

--

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Gateway PoC — timeline update

Laura / Marissa — forwarding Gateway's note. Summary: leadership froze new AI work for Q3; decision-makers traveling; want to push demo to Oct. They asked for a one-pager to keep things warm.

Suggested next steps:
1) Offer a small, non-recoupable credit or a 90-day sandbox to keep momentum without requiring procurement now.
2) Move deal stage to "Nurture/Backlog" in HubSpot and tag as "Q3-deprioritized".
3) Prep a concise one-pager (latency/cost bullets + 3 suggested prompt examples for their workload) and a short Loom walkthrough to send to Elena this week.

If we do a credit, I'm thinking something conservative (e.g., $2k or a $3k pilot credit) — we should avoid opening large discount vectors at this stage. Marissa, can you draft proposed credit terms? Attaching a starter doc.

Thanks —
Jonas

[Attachment: proposed_credit_terms.docx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Gateway PoC — timeline update

Jonas — thanks for the context. Agreed on a light touch approach. Please proceed with the one-pager + Loom and mark the deal as Nurture in HubSpot (use tag: deprioritized-q3).

Credit guidance: approve up to a $2,000 pilot credit or a 90-day sandbox with limited capacity (no SLA changes, no extended support). If Procurement pushes for a larger discount, escalate to me — do not commit additional dollars without approval.

I'll update the revenue owner and set a calendar reminder to re-check in the first week of October. Let's keep it warm; don't log this as a lost deal yet.

—Laura Bennett
VP Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
